title: feat(plugin-approvals,rest,client): a record-anchored approval lock read, `{ locked }` for every caller who can read the record
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X38EQhJnKnxazCiq8xQpv9c)_

Fixes #26314

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

#25934 ruling A ("readers"): the record lock gets a carrier of its own, so a member who can read a record but is not on its approval is no longer offered an edit the server then refuses with `409 RECORD_LOCKED`.

- **`@objectstack/spec`**: one optional member on `IApprovalService`, `getRecordLock?(object, recordId, context): Promise<{ locked: boolean } | null>`, with its doc block. No schema, no exported type.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`**: `ApprovalService.getRecordLock` reads the record **as the caller** (`engine.find` with the caller's context, `fields: ['id']`, `limit: 1`). An unreadable record answers `null`, the same as a missing id; a caller refused the object's read is refused for every id. `locked` comes from the pending-request lookup the hook already uses.
- **One lock judgement**: `nodeConfigLocksRecord(config)` (`lockRecord !== false`) in `lifecycle-hooks.ts` is now the only spelling. The `beforeUpdate` record-lock hook, the request row's `lock_record` mirror and the new read all call it; the read goes through `recordHeldByLockingApproval`, which shares the hook's lookup and its bookkeeping-object exemption.
- **`@objectstack/rest`**: `GET /api/v1/approvals/records/:object/:recordId/lock` answers `{ success: true, data: { locked } }` and nothing else. Every `null` answers one `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` body, so an unreadable record and a missing one cannot be told apart. The closed query-parameter set is empty (route rule 5). A service without the member answers `501`. Ledgered as `sdk`.
- **`@objectstack/client`**: `client.approvals.getRecordLock(object, recordId)`.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` gains a "Reading the lock" paragraph with a curl example.

#8652's ruling is untouched: request content stays behind `approvalsVisibleToReaders`, and the tests assert the non-participant still gets no request row.

## Spec change: needs the spec seat's sign-off

The only `packages/spec/**` change is `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`, new lines 935–972: the doc block plus the optional member `getRecordLock?` inserted right after `getRequest(...)` in `IApprovalService`. Nothing else under `packages/spec/` changed. It is optional so existing implementations and the spec's own `minimalService` literal still satisfy the contract.

## Tests

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-record-lock-read.dogfood.test.ts` (new): the card's four cases through the REST door on a real boot with the real `SecurityPlugin`, flows and approvals plugin, on two `private` objects:
  1. a non-participant who can read and edit the held record gets exactly `{ success: true, data: { locked: true } }`, still gets `[]` from the request list, and their `PATCH` is still `409 RECORD_LOCKED`;
  2. a read-only reader gets `{ locked: true }`;
  3. a caller who cannot read the record (their `GET /data` is 404) gets the same status and body as for a non-existent id (`404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`);
  4. a pending node with `lockRecord: false`, and the held record after approval, both read `{ locked: false }` and the edit lands.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/record-lock-read.integration.test.ts` (new, 4 tests): real ObjectQL over SQLite with the real plugin start; also pins `lock_record` and the read agreeing on every request.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-approvals-record-lock-route.test.ts` (new, 5 tests): preservation (extra keys from a service are dropped), one 404 body for every `null`, the empty closed query set, `501`, and a `403` relay.
- `packages/client/src/client.test.ts`: URL encoding and envelope unwrapping.
- `packages/rest/src/execctx-consumer-census.test.ts`: counts move by one for the new route.

Dogfood does not run on PR CI, so it was run locally under the verify lock.

At head `6ba5f8cc`: plugin-approvals 99 files / 1280 tests pass, client 52 / 672 pass, the new dogfood file 1 / 1 pass. Rest (324 files / 6483 pass, 326 skipped) and spec (725 files / 21974 pass) ran at `99f67d74`; the later merges of `main` changed no file in either package.

### Gates

- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 114 commands; all 114 ran at `6ba5f8cc` with exit 0, reconciled with `--ran` (114 run, 0 not measured, 0 unrun). `main` moved 13 commits during the run; none touches a file in this diff.
- `typecheck` on spec, plugin-approvals, rest and client: exit 0. Spec `check:generated`: exit 0.
- `test:repo` on core, objectql, rest, runtime, spec and types: exit 0.
- Scoped `eslint` over the touched files and `check-nul-bytes`: exit 0.

### Ablations (through the REST door, dogfood)

1. Lock judgement mutated to always lock: red at `approval-record-lock-read.dogfood.test.ts:217`, expected `locked: false` for the `lockRecord: false` record, received `true`. Restored, blob equals HEAD.
2. As-caller read mutated to a system context: red at `:209`, expected `404` for the caller who cannot read the record, received `200`. Restored, blob equals HEAD.

Each mutation was rebuilt into `dist` and confirmed on disk by `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` before the run, and `--absent` after the restore. Ablation 2's declaration build failed (TS6133, `context` unused once the mutation dropped its use); the JS build still carried the mutation, which the preflight found in both `index.js` and `index.mjs`, so the run is valid.

## Deviations from the claim

- The claim named plugin-approvals; the route, ledger row and client method live in `packages/rest` (`approvals-routes.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`) and `packages/client/src/index.ts`. Agreed with the dispatching seat before the change so the ledger row ships as `sdk`, not as a gap.
- Skill teaching is not in this PR: `skills/**` is a governed surface and would make the whole PR need maintainer approval. A follow-up card is named in the report.

## Acceptance notes

- `pendingRequestFor` reads with `limit: 1`, so with two pending requests on one record the hook judges only the first one it gets. The new read reuses the same lookup, so the two still agree; whether two pending requests on one record can happen is not verified here.
- Overlap: open #26337 also edits `approval-service.ts` (different regions) and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` (a nearby section); whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase.
